alignments.note: Connective καί → And.
Article realized as the (rule 19).

Subject noun of the verbless clause; bare tongue. Rule 63 keeps the supplied copula with the predicate nominal rather than with a noun subject, so is goes to πῦρ, exactly as πνεῦμα ὁ θεός → God is a Spirit does.

Predicate nominal of the verbless clause takes the supplied copula under rules 53 and 63; the Greek is anarthrous, so the supplied a is an ordinary rule 7/51 helper on the noun. Head on fire, the word glossing the lexeme.
Article realized as the (rule 19).
κόσμος → world.
The ASV gives iniquity no determiner, so this article has no the to anchor: rule 23, and rule 21 forbids leaving a bare of on it.
Genitive noun rendered of + noun; the case preposition stays with the noun under rule 21's determinerless clause. Head on the noun (rule 17).
Article realized as the (rule 19). Rule 31's article-follows-noun clause leaves the determiner here, on the noun's own preceding article, and gives the trailing ἡ (s016) nothing.
γλῶσσα → tongue. This is the expressed head noun that the participial phrase ἡ σπιλοῦσα modifies and that the ASV's which relativizes.

καθίσταται rendered by the single verb is (ASV: the world of iniquity among our members is the tongue). Discontinuous from its subject under rule 15; the verb is expressed here, so no copula question arises.
ἐν → among (rule 36: the English preposition governing the phrase realizes the Greek preposition).
Rule 20 proper: the free genitive ἡμῶν takes the supplied possessive our, so the article realizes nothing. Rule 76 does not apply, ἡμῶν having no other English of its own.
Genitive pronoun rendered by the possessive our (rule 20).
μέλεσιν → members; the expressed ἐν already carries among, so the noun stands bare.

Second attributive article after its expressed head noun ἡ γλῶσσα, rendered by a finite relative clause: rule 31 makes the relativizer a helper on the participle and leaves this article its own unrepresented unit, as τὴν δύναμιν τὴν ἐνεργουμένην → the power that worketh and τῷ θεῷ τῷ κτίσαντι → God who created do. The competing reading is rule 90's — take ἡ σπιλοῦσα as substantival and give it which — but rule 90 blesses no unit in which a head noun is expressed, and one is: γλῶσσα (s010) stands in the same clause, agrees with this article in gender, number and case, and is the antecedent of the ASV's which. The verse's own alternative_rendering notes confirm the construal, spelling the substantival reading out as that which; the ASV's main text writes a plain relative on an expressed antecedent instead. The intervening καθίσταται ἐν τοῖς μέλεσιν ἡμῶν is discontinuity only, which rules 15 and 57 permit.
Attributive participle rendered as a finite relative clause: the relativizer which is a rule 7 helper on the participle under rule 31, headed on the lexical verb defileth under rules 9 and 17.
Article realized as the (rule 19); split from its noun and from ὅλον under rules 13 and 26.
ὅλον → whole; a Greek article is present to take the determiner, so the adjective stands bare (rule 58).
σῶμα → body.
Expressed conjunction → and.

`φλογίζουσα` rendered by the whole phrase *setteth on fire*. Head on *fire*, the meaning-bearing complement carrying the `φλογ-` lexeme's sense, as rule 17 heads *make straight* on *straight* and rule 91 heads *make known* on *known*; a head on *setteth* would rest only on its being the finite word, which rule 17 refuses. `φλογίζω` occurs nowhere in the corpus outside this verse and `πυρόω` nowhere at all, so rule 91's lemma query returns nothing and the frame query decides instead: where one source verb is rendered by English *set* plus a complement the corpus heads the complement without exception — `ἠλευθέρωσεν` → *did set free* on *free* (GAL.5.1), `ἐσφράγισεν` → *hath set his seal* on *seal* (JHN.3.33), `ἀθετοῦσιν` → *set at nought* on *nought* (JUD.1.8), `ἐλπίσατε` → *and set your hope* on *hope* (1PE.1.13, JHN.5.45), and `πυρούμενοι` → *being on fire* on *fire* (2PE.3.12). The units that do head on *set* are rule 91's contrast working correctly, their lexemes meaning set or establish. JAS.3.10's `ἐξέρχεται` → *cometh forth* headed on *cometh* is consistent rather than in tension: `ἔρχομαι` means *come*, so there the verb word glosses the lexeme.
Article realized as the (rule 19).
τροχόν → wheel.
The ASV gives nature no determiner, so this article has no the to anchor (rule 23).
Genitive noun rendered of + nature; the case preposition rides with the noun under rule 21's determinerless clause, headed on the noun.
Expressed conjunction → and. The bracketed itself of the gloss has no ASV realization and is not aligned.

Passive participle → *is set on fire*; the auxiliary rides inside the unit under rule 9. Head on *fire*, matching the active `φλογίζουσα` above (rule 24) and the corpus's *set* + complement frame cited there.
Agentive ὑπό → by (rule 36).
Article before γεέννης, which the ASV renders by a bare hell with no determiner supplied (rule 23).
γεέννης → hell (the greek_gloss note records Gehenna and changes no correspondence).

review_notes: Corrected s016/s017. The accepted alignment read ἡ σπιλοῦσα as a substantival article under rule 90, giving which to the article and defileth to the participle. Rule 90 disclaims that in terms — it blesses no unit in which a head noun is expressed — and one is expressed here: γλῶσσα (s010) stands in the same clause, agrees with the article in gender, number and case, and is the antecedent the ASV's which relativizes. The construction is rule 31's second attributive article, so the article is unrepresented and which is a helper on the participle, headed on defileth.

The verse's own alternative_rendering notes are the decisive evidence for that change: both spell the substantival construal out as 'that which', which is what the ASV would have written had it read ἡ σπιλοῦσα as rule 90's shape. Its main text writes a plain relative on an expressed antecedent instead, which is rule 31's τῷ θεῷ τῷ κτίσαντι → God who created.

The discontinuity between γλῶσσα and its trailing article (καθίσταται ἐν τοῖς μέλεσιν ἡμῶν intervening) does not defeat the expressed-head-noun test: rule 15 permits a discontinuous unit and rule 57 has an attributive article governing its head noun across whatever stands between them.

Clause division follows the ASV's punctuation and is unchanged: the tongue is a fire is one verbless clause with rule 63 putting the supplied is on the predicate nominal fire, and καθίσταται supplies the second clause's own expressed verb, so no second copula is supplied anywhere.

Both φλογίζω units head on fire rather than on the finite verb word, under rule 17's meaning-bearing-complement clause, keeping the active and passive analyses identical under rule 24. The lexeme is unattested elsewhere in the corpus, so rule 91's query returns nothing and the head rests on the make straight / make known analogy; a later reader with corpus evidence for φλογίζω should check it.

Every article is decided separately (rule 13): s002, s005, s009, s019, s023 take the ASV's the; s007, s025, s030 are unrepresented for want of a determiner; s013 is emptied by the free genitive ἡμῶν under rule 20; s016 is now unrepresented under rule 31. No article in this verse is aligned to a relativizer.
A reference comparison will report s016 as an unrepresented article and therefore as a disagreement with the rule 90 reading; the note on that unit names the competing analysis.
